nodes.label: Guest Mode Pattern (CLAUDE.md)
nodes.rationale: App is browse-first: AppNavigator always mounts public screens, only Settings is gated. Two conventions cover gating: RequireAuth wraps whole screens with no meaningful guest view; useRequireAuth's requireAuth(action) gates a single onPress action on an otherwise-public screen. Chosen because a mobile app without a login-only paywall generally wants people looking around before committing to an account.

nodes.label: navigate() helper
nodes.rationale: Exists because Navbar.tsx is rendered as a Navigator sibling, not a Screen descendant, so useNavigation()/useNavigationState() can't reach the navigator context there; this imperative ref works from anywhere.

nodes.label: AppLockScreen
nodes.rationale: Full-screen PIN gate on launch/foreground; is the actual enforcement point for App Lock, unlike the Settings toggle which only configures it.

nodes.label: SettingsScreen.ProfileSection
nodes.rationale: Resyncs editable name field via compare-and-set during render (React's documented 'adjusting state when a prop changes' pattern) instead of useEffect, to avoid an extra render on every keystroke.

nodes.label: SettingsScreen.DebugSection
nodes.rationale: Plain fetch() against GET /examples/ping, deliberately unabstracted as a copy-paste starting point for wiring any future backend route.

nodes.label: VerifyPinModal
nodes.rationale: Attempt counter/lockout state for PIN verification is owned by SettingsScreen (the parent), not this modal, so closing/reopening the modal doesn't reset the counter -- the modal unmounts its own state when hidden.

nodes.label: AppLockGate
nodes.rationale: Wraps the whole navigator unconditionally but stays inert for guests, since a PIN can only be created from the gated Settings account flow -- so a guest can never have one configured.

nodes.label: Guest-first navigation (design decision)
nodes.rationale: Replaced a fully-authenticated-vs-unauthenticated root switch (no browsable screen without signing up) with per-screen/per-action gating via RequireAuth/useRequireAuth.

nodes.label: NativeWind actually wired up (design decision)
nodes.rationale: NativeWind was in package.json from scaffolding but missing babel/metro config, so every className was inert and screens hand-rolled StyleSheet with duplicated hex colors; fixing the wiring (not a cosmetic pass) was the real fix.

nodes.label: Manual dark-mode toggle via NativeWind colorScheme API (design decision)
nodes.rationale: NativeWind v4 has no CSS custom properties on native, so colorScheme.set()/useColorScheme() is reused instead of building a second, parallel theme context.

nodes.label: Guest-first navigation design
nodes.rationale: No split between a fully-public and fully-authenticated navigator; only the initial route branches on auth state (Home vs Dashboard). Beyond that, no screen is gated by default -- Settings itself turned out to hold mostly guest-relevant content, so only its account-specific sections check isAuthenticated. RequireAuth/useRequireAuth exist as the two conventions a product reaches for once it has something that truly needs a session, even though nothing in the bare template currently calls either.

nodes.label: ADR-006: polling, no realtime in v1
nodes.rationale: Unread notification count is polled on an interval (30s) rather than pushed via realtime/websocket, per ADR-006 -- simpler for v1, no realtime infra needed.
nodes.norm_label: adr-006: polling, no realtime in v1

nodes.label: ADR-008: palette derivation, no WCAG enforcement
nodes.rationale: Custom palettes derive card/muted/border/foreground tokens from 3 anchor colors via fixed color-mix math; deliberately no WCAG contrast enforcement, so a user can pick low-contrast anchors -- accepted as out of scope. destructive/success colors are also fixed outside the palette so danger/success never drift with the chosen accent.
nodes.norm_label: adr-008: palette derivation, no wcag enforcement

nodes.label: ADR-009: single language registry, RTL out of scope
nodes.rationale: supportedLanguages.ts is the single source of truth the Language union derives from, shared with the website template. All current languages are LTR; RTL/Arabic support is deliberately deferred to a future scope. Legal translation copy stays DE/EN-only by design (juristisch geprueft), with other languages falling back to English and a visible banner.
